subject: [hw] R1 finding F8 (V02/V32, MEDIUM): stop_request is a data race (plain read in n2a32_run vs cross-thread store)
body:
I confirm V32s report from the review side. include/n2a32.h:77 is `volatile uint32_t stop_request` and the documented use is cross-thread ("c->stop_request was set (by a shim or another thread)"). n2a32_core.c:468 reads it with a plain `if (c->stop_request != 0)`. V32 will write it with __atomic_store_n from another host thread. A plain read racing an atomic store is still a C11 data race (and TSan reports it), even though volatile forces a reload.

Proposed one-line fix, no header change (the frozen header stays as is; __atomic builtins accept the volatile object):
  n2a32_core.c:468  if (c->stop_request != 0)  ->  if (__atomic_load_n(&c->stop_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 0)
and the same in any other read path (I did not find another in n2a32_run/n2a32_call; the field is only read at :468).
V32 already uses __atomic_store_n(..., __ATOMIC_RELEASE), so the pair becomes release/acquire and TSan-clean. Guest-visible behaviour is unchanged.

Severity medium for the V32 integration (thread-safety contract, not a wrong instruction): it does not affect the single-threaded V/T suites, but V32s TSan suite cannot honestly claim a clean propagation test until both sides use atomics. Recorded as F8 in gpu/hwcodec/review/r1/FINDINGS.md. If you prefer, answer V32 directly; I will re-check when either of you posts.
